description: baseline

Batched one-sided block-Jacobi targeting the dominant large-n shapes (n=512 b=640, n=1024 b=60). Use Brent-Luk round-robin block-pair ordering with a FIXED small sweep count and no per-matrix convergence test; apply the block rotations as batched FP16/TF32 tensor-core GEMMs across the whole batch; per-matrix norm pre-scaling for the high/low-magnitude cases; recover eigenvalue signs via Rayleigh quotient. Finish with one FP32 Newton-Schulz orthonormalization of Q and ascending-sorted L.

Batched two-sided block-Jacobi, bw=16 (2bw=32 hits cuSOLVER batched syevj), Brent-Luk round-robin, rotations as batched GEMMs over (B,p), 10-20 sweeps. Per-block diagonalization correct and V stays orthogonal/consistent (V^T A V == Acur), but off-diagonal Frobenius STAGNATES at nonzero fixed point (block-identity drift: eigh re-sorts within each 2bw block each round). Diagonal/identity pass; all dense Jacobi-path cases fail eigen-residual by ~1e4x. Diagnosed: convergence restored by reordering eigvec columns via a VALID greedy closest-to-identity permutation (offF 1e-3, eig_err 1e-2 at n=512 in 8 sweeps).

Convergent block-Jacobi: added valid greedy closest-to-identity eigvec-column permutation per 2bw block -> ALL 39 validation tests PASS (correctness solved). But the greedy stabilization is a 32-iteration Python loop with ~4 small-kernel launches each, called R*sweeps (~3800) times per timed call => millions of kernel launches. Benchmark still on shape 2 (n=352) after 17 min, far slower than baseline; killed. Fallback shapes 0/1 (n=32,176) matched baseline. Next: replace greedy loop with a launch-light vectorized stabilization (argsort-of-argmax) and route the A/V update GEMMs through TF32/BF16.

Cheap argsort stabilization makes block-Jacobi benchmarkable: 724718us geomean, all shapes pass. But 2.8x SLOWER than baseline (255037). nsys on n512b640: 41% of GPU time is gather/index_select+elementwise (the per-round double permutation of the full (B,n,n) A and reshapes), only 13% is the rotation GEMMs (which are SIMT cutlass sgemm, NOT tensor core). Memory/launch-bound: ~20 kernels x 372 rounds. n=32/176 shapes 3-32x FASTER (fallback). Levers: (1) eliminate per-round full-A permutation, (2) fewer sweeps (n512 converges at 8), (3) TF32/bigger GEMMs for tensor cores.

Added the brief's final polish: one FP32 Newton-Schulz reorthonormalization of Q (Q<-Q(1.5I-0.5 Q^T Q)) + eigenvalues via FP32 Rayleigh quotient L=diag(Q^T A Q) (computed as (V*(A@V)).sum), plus adaptive sweeps (10 for n<=512, 11 for 1024, 12 else). All 39 tests pass; 654818us geomean (10% faster than iter3's 724718, still 2.6x slower than baseline 255037). NOTE: tried global TF32 (allow_tf32) on the sweep GEMMs - it broke orthogonality AND eigen-residual (300-800x over) even with reorthonorm at 8 sweeps; reverted. Bottleneck remains per-round full-(B,n,n) gather/permute (41% in iter3 profile), not the GEMMs (13%, SIMT). Next: persistent permuted layout (verified composed transition-permutation halves gather) + selectively-safe reduced precision.

Persistent permuted layout: keep the working matrix and V in pair-blocked layout across the whole sweep and apply only the composed round->round transition permutation once per round (instead of permute->work->unpermute = 4 index_selects/round on the full (B,n,n) A). Bookkeeping (pos2orig tracking + final row un-permute) verified: all 39 tests pass. 582249us geomean, 11% faster than iter4 (654818); n512 3.2M, n1024 2.1M. Still ~2.3x slower than baseline. Next: TF32/bf16 on the working-matrix update GEMMs (V stays FP32-accumulated + final Newton-Schulz + Rayleigh L recover precision), and profile to confirm GEMM vs eigh vs residual gather split.

bw=32 block-Jacobi + per-matrix prescale + n-adaptive sweeps (n<=512:11 for clustered convergence, n<=1024:9). VALIDATED (all 39 tests pass). Benchmark reported 1991146us BUT this is heavily CONTENTION-INFLATED: the run overlapped 5-6 other fleet benchmarks saturating the shared B200 board. Proof: shape 2 (n=352) takes the cuSOLVER FALLBACK path (pure torch.linalg.eigh, identical to baseline code) yet measured 1,523,352us vs its 58,122us idle baseline = 26x inflation from contention alone; shape 3 (n512) 11.7M vs iter5's 3.2M = 3.6x. The TRUE bw=32 speed is ~30% faster than iter5's bw=16 per a clean isolated diagnostic (n512: bw32 1857ms vs bw16 2574ms; n1024: 1029 vs 1567ms). Metric not comparable to idle baseline/earlier iters due to contention.

Brief 0 (batched block-Jacobi) exhausted. Built a fully-batched two-sided block-Jacobi eigensolver (Brent-Luk round-robin, fixed sweeps, batched-GEMM rotations over (B,p), FP32 Newton-Schulz reorthonormalization, FP32 Rayleigh-quotient L, per-matrix prescaling). Solved 2 hard sub-problems: (1) naive block-Jacobi STAGNATES (block-identity drift from eigh re-sorting) - fixed with a valid closest-to-identity eigvec-column permutation; (2) FP32 breakdown on extreme-magnitude LAPACK cases - fixed by per-matrix prescale to O(1). Clean idle-measured progression: 724k -> 654k -> 582k us; bw=32 then ~30% faster than bw=16 in isolated diagnostic (n512 1857 vs 2574ms). CRITICAL FINDING (invalidates brief premise): PyTorch torch.linalg.eigh on 2bw-batched blocks does NOT use cuSOLVER batched-syevj - it uses heavy divide-and-conquer (sytrd+laed4) = ~40-50% of GPU time. Block-Jacobi does ~10x a direct solver's flops and is eigh-bound, so best case is ~parity-to-1.6x-slower than the 255k baseline. The iter7 benchmark (1.99M us) is CONTENTION-INFLATED ~4-26x (fleet ran 5-6 concurrent benchmarks; the cuSOLVER-fallback n=352 shape alone was 26x its idle baseline) and is NOT comparable. Best safe committed = iter7 (629818d, bw=32, validated). SUGGESTIONS for next briefs: (a) replace the inner 2bw eigh with a custom closed-form/few-step Jacobi 32x32 solve to break the eigh bottleneck (biggest lever); (b) bf16 GEMMs now worth ~24% at bw=32 (V stays FP32 + reorthonorm); (c) try bw=64; (d) the env-suggested GEMM-heavy alternatives (QDWH/Zolo spectral D&C, batched tridiag->D&C) that avoid per-round eigh entirely. INFRA: fleet GPU contention is inflating all benchmarks 4-26x - idle isolation is needed for comparable numbers.

Fork W1's validated GEMM-only matrix-sign spectral D&C (c0161ccb8) and kill its LEAF bottleneck — the recursion bottoms out at torch.linalg.eigh on small blocks, which you proved uses heavy D&C (sytrd4_cta+laed4_par, 40-50% of time) instead of a fast path. Replace that leaf eigh with a custom FAST batched small-matrix (<=32-64) symmetric solver: a fixed-sweep two-sided Jacobi entirely in registers/SMEM (your closest-to-identity permutation fix + per-matrix prescale port directly), or an analytic path for the tiniest blocks, so the many small leaf solves run as one cheap batched kernel rather than cuSOLVER D&C. Also tune the recursion cutoff (stop recursing when a batched direct solve on the block wins) and stabilize the deflation. Apply set_float32_matmul_precision('high') to the bmm. Emit FP32 Q ascending; benchmark clean min-of-3.

Deferred-leaf-gather: restructured W1's recursion into a forward _build_tree (computes V's once, COLLECTS every leaf block padded to 32) + ONE batched scalar-Jacobi leaf solve + bottom-up _materialize. Replaces W1's 6330 tiny cuSOLVER eigh calls (probe: 6330 leaf calls, 14696 matrices, avg B~2.3, mostly B=1!) with one batched solve. Plus TF32 front-end + FP32 final polish (TF32 broke the orthogonality gate). VALIDATES all 39 tests. But benchmark TOO SLOW: n=32 76ms (16x baseline), n=176 492ms (25x), stuck >219s on n=512 -> killed. Two causes: (1) the PyTorch scalar-Jacobi leaf is LAUNCH-BOUND (12 sweeps x 31 rounds = ~3300 kernel launches, ~66ms flat tax), (2) W1's front-end FRAGMENTS the batch into thousands of B=1 nodes (groups-by-k at every level) so the sign-iteration GEMMs/QR are launch-bound too. Next: (a) custom CUDA leaf Jacobi (one launch, SMEM-resident) per brief; (b) RAISE the leaf cutoff (defragments recursion - shallower = fewer B=1 nodes, helps front-end too, in-brief 'tune cutoff').

Custom CUDA SMEM-resident batched Jacobi leaf kernel (one block/matrix, ONE launch for whole leaf batch) + leaf-gather + LEAF=64 + DirectLeaf jitter safety. VALIDATES all 39. The LEAF is now FAST: n=32 (pure leaf path) benchmarks 3514us vs baseline 4586us (FASTER; vs iter1 PyTorch-leaf 76397us = 22x leaf speedup). KEY: I had to REMOVE the global TF32 (set_float32_matmul_precision high) - it DESTABILIZES W1's matrix-sign front-end on ill-conditioned spectra: the Newton-Schulz iteration can't resolve eigenvalues near the split sigma -> wrong rank k -> non-shrinking recursion to the depth cap -> cuSOLVER eigh then fails (err 370) even with jitter. FP32 front-end restores W1's validated behavior. BUT benchmark still too slow on n>=176 (stuck >126s on n=176): W1's front-end fragments into ~2420 B=1 QR/GEMM calls (LEAF=64) -> launch-bound, dominates my branch. Killed. The leaf is my deliverable for the W5 combine; front-end is W5's. Next: LEAF=96 (probe: 1074 QR calls, 2.3x less) needs dynamic-SMEM kernel.

LEAF=96 via dynamic-SMEM (opt-in, cudaFuncAttributeMaxDynamicSharedMemorySize) CUDA Jacobi kernel. VALIDATES all 39. Now BENCHMARKABLE (iter1/iter2 were too slow to complete): geomean 2271225us. The custom CUDA leaf solver WORKS and the larger cutoff cut front-end fragmentation 8.3x (1074 vs 8930 QR calls vs orig LEAF=32). BUT still ~8.9x slower than baseline (255037): the n=512 b=640 shapes are 13-15M us (~25x baseline) because W1's FP32 matrix-sign front-end STILL fragments ~1074 B=1 QR/GEMM nodes -> launch-bound, and it dominates. This is contention-inflated too (fleet busy). My LEAF deliverable is correct+fast (the leaf solve itself is one cheap kernel); the front-end fragmentation is W5's domain and the binding bottleneck. CRITICAL cross-cutting finding: global TF32 (set_float32_matmul_precision high) DESTABILIZES W1's sign-iteration rank-split on ill-conditioned spectra (non-shrinking recursion -> crash); had to keep FP32 front-end. The leaf composes with W5's tensor-core front-end via combine.

Brief 1 (kill W1's leaf bottleneck) exhausted. DELIVERED: a custom CUDA SMEM-resident batched two-sided Jacobi leaf solver (dynamic shared memory / opt-in, handles n<=128, one block/matrix, ONE kernel launch for the whole leaf batch) that replaces W1's torch.linalg.eigh leaf, PLUS a deferred-leaf-gather restructure (forward _build_tree collects all leaf blocks -> ONE batched solve -> bottom-up _materialize, eliminating W1's 6330 tiny per-node eigh calls), PLUS leaf-cutoff tuning to 96 (8.3x less front-end fragmentation), PLUS a DirectLeaf+jitter safety net for depth-cap escapes. All 39 tests validate; geomean 2271225us. PROFILE-PROVEN OUTCOME: my jacobi_batched_kernel is now only 0.8% of GPU time (ONE launch, ~100ms), while the BINDING bottleneck is the QR in _range_basis: geqr2_smem_domino_fast 43.8% (13947 instances!) + geqr2_batch_kernel 35.1% = ~79% of time is QR decompositions in the front-end's randomized subspace iteration, which fragments into thousands of B=1 calls. The leaf is solved; the front-end QR/fragmentation is W5's domain and the real wall. My leaf composes into the lineage via the W5 combine (then the leaf is free and the front-end QR is the target). CRITICAL CROSS-CUTTING FINDING for the fleet: global TF32 (set_float32_matmul_precision high) DESTABILIZES W1's matrix-sign front-end on ill-conditioned spectra - the Newton-Schulz iteration can't resolve eigenvalues near the split point sigma, giving a wrong rank k and a non-shrinking recursion that runs to the depth cap where even cuSOLVER eigh fails (err 370). I had to keep FP32 front-end. W5 must use a precision-robust sign iteration (or a different rank estimator) before applying TF32. SUGGEST next: a worker should attack _range_basis - replace the per-group randomized-QR subspace iteration (79%, 13947 QR launches) with either a batched/fused QR or a projector-application that avoids QR, OR defragment the groups-by-k into padded uniform batched sub-calls. All benchmarks remain contention-inflated (fleet busy).

The sign-D&C lineage is dead (you, W1, W5, W4 all proved it). Redeploy your custom-CUDA SMEM-resident batched-Jacobi expertise onto the ONE clean separable seam of the direct two-stage dense solver W1 is building: the batched TRIDIAGONAL eigensolve. A symmetric tridiagonal T is the ultimate banded matrix — your leaf kernel (one launch, SMEM-resident, n<=128) extends naturally to it. Build a fast batched symmetric-tridiagonal eigensolver for n=512/1024: input the (B,n) diagonal + (B,n-1) off-diagonal from W1's tridiagonalization, output eigenvalues (ascending) + the tridiagonal eigenvectors S, as ONE batched kernel — fixed-sweep tridiagonal-QL/PWK or bisection+inverse-iteration in SMEM/registers, no per-matrix cuSOLVER calls, no launch storm. Clean numeric contract (T -> (eigvals, S)) so it composes into W1's solver via combine with zero ABI friction. TF32 is fine here (W2's own finding: TF32 is safe for the leaf, fatal only for the sign rank-split which this approach doesn't have). Emit FP32 outputs; benchmark clean idle min-of-3.

Direct two-stage solver: Householder tridiag (PyTorch placeholder) + CUSTOM CUDA batched tridiagonal eigensolver (bisection via Sturm sequences for eigenvalues + inverse iteration via Thomas for eigenvectors + STEIN-style reorthogonalized inverse iteration for clusters: orthogonalize-then-reiterate, which fixes the cluster collapse plain inverse iteration suffers) + back-transform + Newton-Schulz polish. Solver isolated-tested MATCHES cuSOLVER on rankdef/nearrank/mixed (res ~2e-4, orth ~5e-4 = torch.eigh-of-T quality). Standalone solver timing 15ms for n=512 b640 (vs baseline full-eigh 556ms). Pipeline VALIDATES all 39 tests. BUT benchmark recheck (shifted seeds) FAILED on shape 7 (n=1024 b60 MIXED, matrix=12): eigen-residual 0.965 vs 0.171 (5.6x over) - a harder mixed sub-matrix the cluster refinement didn't fully resolve. Per-shape so far: n=32 4865us (~baseline), n=176 26412us (1.36x). Next: strengthen cluster robustness (more inv-iters/refine passes) and/or FP32 tridiagonalization for n=1024.

ROBUST direct two-stage eigensolver, ALL 39 validate + benchmark passes: geomean 921984us. Stage 2 (my deliverable) = custom CUDA batched tridiagonal eigensolver: bisection (Sturm) for eigenvalues + inverse iteration (Thomas) for eigenvectors + STEIN-style reorthogonalized inverse iteration for clusters + residual-AND-orthogonality-checked cuSOLVER fallback for the rare pathological matrix (diagonal-geometric tail below FP32 floor; hard mixed sub-matrices). Standalone solver: 15ms for n=512 b640 (vs baseline full-eigh 556ms = 37x). Also fixed: prescaled Rayleigh quotient (FP32 q^T A q on raw 1e19 A loses the small eigenvalues). The 922k geomean is dominated by the PLACEHOLDER per-column Householder tridiagonalization (launch-bound, W1's domain) + the per-call residual+orth check GEMMs + cuSOLVER fallback on clustered shapes; my tridiagonal solver is a small fraction. n512 dense 1.79M, n512 lapack_dense 896k (1.36x baseline). Composes with W1's fast tridiagonalization via combine.

Brief 2 (batched tridiagonal eigensolver) DONE. DELIVERED: a custom CUDA batched symmetric-tridiagonal eigensolver (input diagonal+off-diagonal -> eigenvalues ascending + eigenvectors S, ONE kernel launch for the whole batch): bisection via Sturm sequences for eigenvalues + inverse iteration via Thomas solves for eigenvectors + STEIN-style reorthogonalized inverse iteration (orthogonalize-then-reiterate) for clusters, with a residual+orthogonality-gated cuSOLVER fallback for the rare pathological matrix. STANDALONE SOLVER TIMING: ~15ms for n=512 b=640 and ~17ms for n=1024 b=60 (vs the baseline's full dense eigh 556ms/598ms for those shapes = ~37x faster). No QL rotation chain (tested: QL-with-vectors was 1587ms, thread-0-serial-bound; bisection+inverse-iteration is 100x faster and fully parallel), no per-matrix cuSOLVER, no launch storm. Full pipeline (placeholder Householder tridiag + my solver + back-transform) VALIDATES all 39 tests; best benchmarked geomean 921984us (iter2, 6751b97d) is dominated ENTIRELY by the launch-bound per-column Householder tridiagonalization placeholder - W1/W5's domain - not my solver. iter3 (40c94e62c, committed+validated) further gates the fallback checks (O(n^2) tridiagonal residual instead of O(n^3) bmm; O(n^3) orthogonality check only on tight-gap matrices) to remove per-call overhead. Numeric contract T->(eigvals,S) is clean, so this composes into W5/W3's fast tridiagonalization+back-transform via combine with zero ABI friction - that's where the lineage wins (fast tridiag + my fast tridiagonal solve, both batched). KEY FINDINGS: (1) clusters/degenerate spectra need stein-style reorthogonalized inverse iteration (plain inverse iteration collapses a cluster to one direction); (2) the Thomas pivot must be clamped to a NORM-RELATIVE floor not 1e-20 (else x~b/1e-20~1e19 overflows FP32 -> rsqrt(Inf)=0 -> all-zero eigenvector on diagonal matrices); (3) Rayleigh L must use the PRESCALED A (raw 1e19 A loses small eigenvalues in FP32). TF32 was fine throughout (no sign rank-split here, confirming my brief-1 finding).

Pair your fast tridiagonal eigensolver (6751b97d, ~15ms) with a fast tridiagonalization you build yourself, making a complete single-worker batched solver. Build a fused single-launch Householder tridiagonalization kernel — one threadblock per matrix, the trailing matrix kept SMEM/register-resident across the whole reduction so there is NO HBM round-trip between panels and NO per-column kernel launch — a distinct design point from W5's panel-block WY GEMM approach (latency-bound single-kernel vs throughput-bound blocked GEMM). Ground it in a quick profile of where cuSOLVER's XsyevBatched actually spends its n=512 b640 time (tridiag vs D&C vs back-transform), so the kernel targets the real cost. Feed its tridiagonal into your solver + a back-transform.

iter0: fused single-launch Householder tridiagonalization kernel (one block/matrix, full reduction internal, in-kernel Qh accumulation) replacing the per-column torch placeholder. All 39 validate. Small-n shapes 2-6x FASTER (launch-bound placeholder gone) but large-n WORSE (n2048 19.2M): one-block-per-matrix + O(n^3) SIMT Qh accumulation serialize at large n.

iter1: kernel outputs reflectors V (not Qh); back-transform Q=H_0..H_{n-3}@S via compact-WY blocked GEMMs (FP32). Removes the in-kernel O(n^3) Qh pass + moves back-transform off SIMT. geomean 911105 (parent 920990); large-n improved but trd_kernel still the large-n bottleneck.

iter2: COALESCE the symv + rank-2 trailing update (warp-per-row, lanes-stride-columns). geomean 566022 (1.6x vs iter1, 1.6x vs parent): n512 lapack_dense 201718 vs 1160403 (5.7x). The trailing-update column stride was the killer.

iter3: BLOCKED latrd (panel + deferred rank-2k syr2k) in the fused kernel. geomean 583899 - SLIGHT REGRESSION vs iter2: blocking helped only the pure-tridiag-bound shape 11 (11%); the per-column deferred-update correction loops + extra syncs cancel the saved WRITE traffic; symv READ traffic unchanged. Reverted kernel to iter2 next.

iter4: TF32 back-transform for n>=512 (eigen gate 200*n*eps loosens with n). geomean 580539 - WASH vs iter2 (within noise): the WY back-transform is only ~16% of tridiag-bound shapes and its skinny-K GEMMs stay SIMT even under TF32. Back-transform not the bottleneck; trd_kernel (latency-bound) is.

iter5: 4-way unroll the symv+update inner loops (4 independent accumulators) to hide the SMEM-load-latency stall (ncu: 82.9% warp cycles stalled on shared-mem scoreboard, latency-bound). geomean 550936 (best so far; vs iter2 566022): n512 lapack 174325 vs 201718 (14%).

iter6: 8-way unroll. geomean 546887 (marginal vs iter5, within noise): 4-way already captured the ILP; ncu shows occupancy dropped to 63.7% (40 reg/thread limits to 3 blocks/SM) - diminishing returns.

iter7: batch the WY back-transform T-factor build across ALL panels at once (stack panels into the batch dim -> nb-step recurrence runs ONCE, not nb-per-panel) - kills the ~512-tiny-bmm launch storm. geomean 524578 (best; parent 920990 = 1.76x): n176 8634 vs 11982 (28%), n352 43240 vs 51120 (15%).

iter8: SYMMETRIC symv+update - read/write only the LOWER triangle (half memory traffic -> less L2/HBM thrash at b640), off-diag scattered to p[c] via SMEM atomicAdd. geomean 542506 - net slight regression vs iter7 BUT BETTER on every large shape (n512 lapack 155994 vs 165319 = 6%); SMEM-atomic contention regresses small shapes. Routed by n next.

iter9: ROUTE symv/update by n - symmetric half-traffic (lower-tri + SMEM-atomic scatter) for n>=256, full-row coalesced 8-way for n<256. geomean 520061 (BEST; parent 920990 = 1.77x): keeps the symmetric large-n win (n512 lapack 149962 = 4.39x faster than baseline 657792) AND restores small-shape speed (n32 1719, n176 8627). PROFILE: on tridiag-bound shape 11 trd_kernel is 53.9% + back-transform 23%; on dense/clustered shapes tri_eig (stage 2, off-brief) is 87.5% and trd_kernel only 7.6%.

Brief 3 (fused single-launch Householder tridiagonalization) DONE. DELIVERED: a complete single-worker batched eigensolver = my fused tridiagonalization (this brief) -> my batched tridiagonal solver (brief 2) -> WY-GEMM back-transform. The tridiagonalization is ONE custom CUDA kernel, ONE launch for the whole batch: one threadblock per matrix runs the ENTIRE Householder reduction internally (all n-2 columns, persistent kernel) with the trailing matrix owned in global memory across the whole reduction - NO per-column kernel launch, NO HBM round-trip / torch trailing GEMM between panels (distinct from W5's panel-block WY-GEMM design). Outputs (d, e, V-reflectors); back-transform applies the reflectors Q=H_0..H_{n-3}@S via compact-WY blocked GEMMs (T-factors built in ONE stacked batched recurrence to kill a per-panel launch storm). Best geomean 520061us (iter9, de6ec33c), validated all 39, = 1.77x faster than the parent 920990 (which used a launch-bound per-column torch placeholder tridiag). PROGRESSION 1102368->911105->566022->...->520061. KEY OPTIMIZATIONS (each measured): (1) coalesce the symv+trailing-update (warp-per-row, lanes-stride-columns) = 1.6x - the stride-n column access was the killer; (2) output reflectors + WY-GEMM back-transform instead of in-kernel O(n^3) Qh accumulation; (3) 4/8-way unroll the inner loops to hide the SMEM-load-latency stall (ncu: 83% of warp cycles were shared-mem scoreboard stalls); (4) batch the WY T-factor build across all panels; (5) SYMMETRIC half-traffic symv/update (lower-triangle-only + SMEM-atomic scatter) routed in for n>=256 (cuts L2/HBM thrash at b640), full-coalesced path for n<256 (avoids atomic contention). MANDATED PROFILE of cuSOLVER XsyevBatched n512 b640 (W0's 88224771 capture): it IS genuinely batched and TRIDIAG-BOUND - sytrd4_cta 21.6% + the gemv/symv panel updates ~41% = ~66% tridiagonalization, D&C (laed*) ~20%, back-transform small - so targeting the tridiag was correct. RESULT: my tridiagonalization is now FAST and NOT the bottleneck - on the pure-tridiag-bound n512 lapack_dense shape my trd_kernel is 4.39x faster than baseline (149962 vs 657792) and the full pipeline beats baseline on shapes 0/1/2/11. THE BINDING WALL is now off-brief: on the geomean-dominant dense/clustered shapes (3,6,7,9,12) my STAGE-2 tri_eig_kernel's sequential thread-0 cluster-refinement is 87.5% of GPU time (trd_kernel only 7.6%) - profile worker-2-brief-3-iteration-9-n512dense-de6ec33c.nsys-rep. n2048 b8 (shape 5, 7.6M) is occupancy-starved (8 matrices = 8 blocks on 148 SMs; single-block-per-matrix cannot fill the GPU; cuSOLVER's multi-block sytrd wins there 12x). SUGGEST next briefs: (a) PARALLELIZE stage-2 cluster refinement - the thread-0-serial Thomas re-solve per cluster is now the dominant cost on dense/clustered n=512/1024; rewrite it warp-parallel or batch the cluster re-solves, the single biggest geomean lever left; (b) a per-(n,batch) ROUTER falling back to cuSOLVER XsyevBatched for n2048-b8 (and any shape where the single-block design is occupancy-starved) while keeping my fast pipeline where it wins; (c) the back-transform's skinny-K=nb rank update GEMM stays SIMT even under TF32 (~23% on tridiag-bound shapes) - a BF16x9/larger-nb tensor-core back-transform could shave it. The fused tridiagonalization composes cleanly into the lineage (clean (A)->(d,e,V) + WY back-transform contract).

You profiled the binding wall: your stage-2 tri_eig_kernel cluster-refinement is 87.5% of GPU time on the dense/clustered shapes — a thread-0-SERIAL Thomas re-solve per clustered eigenvalue. The benchmark's dense/clustered/lapack shapes have tightly-clustered spectra, so this serial cluster path dominates. Parallelize it: spread the per-cluster reorthogonalized inverse-iteration / Thomas solves across the warp/threads (one thread or lane per cluster member, batched modified-Gram-Schmidt instead of the serial re-solve), or replace the cluster handling with a small dense eigensolve on the cluster's projected block. This is the single biggest remaining lever for the custom two-stage path, and the same clustered-eigenvalue wall blocks the other combine workers. Keep your fast tridiagonalization + WY back-transform.

iter0: PARALLELIZED the stage-2 cluster refinement (the brief). Replaced the thread-0-SERIAL Thomas re-solve per clustered column (was 87.5% of GPU time on dense/clustered/lapack shapes) with a fully block-parallel stein-style refinement: cluster members inverse-iterated IN PARALLEL (one thread/column, own Thomas solve) + CGS2 reorthonormalization (per column all m earlier-member dots at once -> O(C) block-syncs/cluster, not MGS O(C^2)). Clusters found by forward scan; CLUSTER_ROUNDS=2; proj reuses e2[] SMEM. All 39 validate; geomean 252595us = 2.06x faster than parent 520062, and FIRST time the custom two-stage BEATS the cuSOLVER baseline (255037). Big shape wins: dense n512 1.79M->552K (3.2x), dense/mixed n1024 improved. Clustered shape9 690K.

iter1: CLUSTER_ROUNDS 2->1. The 2nd refinement round (re-iterate+CGS2) was redundant - cluster eigenvalues are ~equal so an orthonormal basis of the phase-1 inverse-iteration vectors IS a valid eigenbasis; a single CGS2 pass-pair delivers it. All 39 validate; geomean 202471us (vs rounds=2 252595 = 1.25x, parent 520062 = 2.57x, baseline 255037 = 1.26x FASTER). (2) The FAST front-end is real but the BAND->TRIDIAG reduction kills it. Per-column MGS with random breakdown-replacement FIXES accuracy (orth 1.5e-4) but is launch-bound (per-column Python loop).
